text:
The idiom “count your chickens before they hatch” warns that if you assume you already have something that hasn’t happened yet, you may end up with nothing at all.  
Among the choices, the statement that most directly captures that warning is:

**(F) You will end up without any chickens**  

It expresses the literal outcome of the idiom – you’ll be left with no chickens (i.e., with nothing) because you relied on something that never materialized.  

**Final answer:** (F)
